narrative_text: Complainant Sudhir Yeolekar, resident of 6, Chhota Bazaar, appeared before the undersigned and stated that on the night of 04/03/2026 he had parked his black Hero Splendor motorcycle outside his residence at approximately 22:30 hrs. On the morning of 05/03/2026 at about 07:15 hrs he found the vehicle missing from the said spot. The complainant states the steering lock was engaged and no broken parts were found at the location. He informs that a similar theft was reported by a neighbour in Chhota Bazaar Lane 3 about a fortnight earlier, however he does not know that complainant's name. The complainant could not provide the chassis number at the time of reporting and has been directed to produce registration papers within three days. Enquiry was made with the tea stall owner opposite the residence who stated that he closed at 23:00 hrs and observed nothing unusual. No CCTV coverage is available on this stretch. Complainant's contact number is available on record. Offence registered and investigation taken up by ASI on duty. Case transferred to Purana Peth crime detection unit for further enquiry.

Complainant Manisha Padhye, working as a lab technician and residing at 57, Devgiri Colony, reports that between 09:00 hrs and 18:30 hrs on 07/03/2026, while she and her family were away attending a function at Devgiri Colony Phase 2, unknown persons broke open the rear kitchen door of her house and removed gold ornaments and cash. The complainant estimates the ornaments to be two bangles, one chain and a pair of ear studs. Cash of approximately eighteen thousand rupees kept in a steel almirah was also taken. The almirah lock was found forced. Neighbours reported seeing a yellow cargo auto parked at the lane end during the afternoon but none noted the registration number. Enquiry was made with the milk supplier of the lane, Sulabha Chaudhari, who stated she completed her round by 08:00 hrs and saw nothing. Finger print unit was called and lifted partial impressions from the almirah handle. Spot panchnama prepared in the presence of two witnesses from the same lane. Investigation continues.

Complainant Smt. Sulabha Chaudhari, milk supplier, resident of 42, Vashisht Market Road, states that in the month of January 2026 she was approached by one D. Kalgutkar who described himself as proprietor of Ashvamedh Trading Solutions, having office at Unit 12, Tilakwadi Commercial Complex, Block C, Nandanvan West. The said person assured her a monthly return of eight per cent on a commodity trading plan and provided a mobile number 9000011012 for contact. On his instruction the complainant transferred rupees ninety eight thousand by UPI to a current account of the said firm. She was issued a receipt bearing a rubber stamp of the firm signed by one lady who introduced herself as the director, Amrapali Deshkulkarni. For the first month a sum was credited back but thereafter payments stopped. When the complainant visited the office in the first week of March the premises were locked. The number 9000011012 is now switched off. Complainant states at least four other persons from Vashisht Market area have been similarly induced. A silver coloured Honda City bearing number MP09CF8823 was seen used by the said Kalgutkar.

Complainant Omkar Bhosalekar, photographer, resident of 230, Vashisht Market Road, submits that he invested rupees one lakh forty five thousand with a firm styled as Ashvamedh Trading Solutions Pvt Ltd on the assurance of one Devanshu R. Kalgutkar. The complainant states that the accounts of the firm were maintained by a woman known to him as R. Nagvekar, who would call from 9000011145 to remind investors of due dates and who visited his studio twice. The complainant produces two printed statements bearing the firm letterhead which he now believes to be fabricated as the registration number printed thereon does not tally with the number available on public record. He further states that on 04/03/2026 he saw the said Kalgutkar loading cartons into a silver Honda City MP09CF8823 outside the Tilakwadi Commercial Complex at about 19:00 hrs, and that a yellow cargo auto bearing MP09EG5507 was also present, driven by a man addressed as Jayendra. On enquiry the complainant was told the office was shifting. Since 08/03/2026 no person is available at the said office. Complainant seeks recovery of his money and action against the firm and its directors.

Complainant Manisha Kanhere of 171, Nandanvan East states that on the evening of 17/03/2026 at about 20:45 hrs a quarrel took place at Shrivardhan Apartments, Nandanvan, over parking of two wheelers in the common lane. The complainant states she had gone to visit her sister residing in the same building when the dispute began between two residents of the ground and third floor. Abusive language was used and one party pushed the other causing a minor injury to the elbow. The complainant states that a resident of Flat 3B, Harsh Vadnere, employed as a software support engineer, intervened and separated the parties, and that he is willing to depose as a witness. The society watchman was present and also witnessed the incident. Medical examination of the injured party was conducted at the government dispensary and a minor abrasion was noted. Both parties are residents of long standing and have no previous record. The complainant has stated she does not wish to press for severe action but wants the matter recorded so that the society committee takes note. Notice issued to both parties for appearance.

On 20/03/2026 at about 00:14 hrs a white Tata 1109 LPT truck bearing registration MP09TJ4471 was intercepted at Rewa Gate Check Post during a routine night check. The driver produced a licence in the name of Samir Tandalekar and stated that he had loaded the consignment at Nandanvan Cold Storage the previous night and that the goods belonged to Kaveri Depot Logistics Pvt Ltd. On inspection the declared manifest showed forty crates of perishable goods, however seventeen crates in the front stack contained cartons of foreign origin without any import documentation. The driver was unable to produce a gate pass and stated on enquiry that he had been instructed by telephone from 9000014417 to reach the check post before 01:00 hrs. Complaint is lodged by the check post duty officer through Head Constable Ritesh Wanjarkhede. The truck stands registered in the name of one R. Mirajkar of Flat 3B, Shrivardhan Apartments, Nandanvan, who is stated to be the supervisor of the said cold storage. A second vehicle, a blue Ashok Leyland MP09QR2208, was reported by the toll operator to have passed twenty minutes ahead of the intercepted truck. Goods seized under panchnama.

Pursuant to information developed in connection with the seizure at Rewa Gate on 20/03/2026, enquiry was conducted at Nandanvan Cold Storage, Plot 7, Nandanvan Industrial Belt. The complainant Ayesha Kharpude, chartered accountant engaged for statutory audit of the storage LLP, has submitted a written complaint stating that stock registers for the period 01/03/2026 to 25/03/2026 do not reconcile with the physical stock and that seventeen inward entries carry no supporting invoice. She names one Tejpal G., a driver attached to the depot and residing at Flat 3B, Shrivardhan Apartments, Nandanvan, who on two occasions signed the gate register on behalf of the consignee without authority. She further states that the consignee shown in those entries is a wholesale concern operated by Vipin K. Sadhwani from Shop 44, Vashisht Market, First Floor, and that payments for these lots were received in a manner not routed through the LLP books. A blue Tata Ace bearing MP09MN6635 was observed by the complainant collecting goods from the rear gate on 24/03/2026 at about 22:00 hrs. Registers seized for examination.

Complainant Dattatray Deolalikar, bank clerk attached to the Purana Peth branch, has reported under branch compliance instructions that account holder Nilesh W., proprietor of a cloth business at 7, Wagholikar Wada, Purana Peth, presented a self cheque for rupees seventeen lakh fifty thousand on 23/03/2026 at about 10:52 hrs and insisted on cash payment. The complainant states that the said sum had been credited to the account only that morning by RTGS from an account held at Chandrabhaga Bank Ltd in the name of one S. Barkatpuri, and that a similar credit of comparable size had been received by the same account through a different intermediary in the last week of February. The complainant states that when asked the purpose of withdrawal the account holder gave the reason as purchase of cloth consignment but could not name the supplier. A white Hyundai i20 bearing MP09AW9014 was waiting outside the branch and the cash was carried to it by a second person. The account holder's mobile 9000011593 was found to be in constant use during the transaction. Branch has placed the account under watch and reported the matter.

Complaint received from Rupesh Barhate, primary teacher residing at 34, Kaveri Depot Workers Colony, who states that for the last several weeks trucks have been entering and leaving the Kaveri Depot Yard between 21:00 and 01:00 hrs and that loading is carried out with the yard lights switched off. He states that on the night of 28/03/2026 he observed a white truck and a blue truck being loaded and that a young man on a black Pulsar motorcycle bearing MP09LD3390 was stationed at the yard gate and questioned anyone approaching. He identifies this person as one Chetan B., a loader residing in the same colony. The complainant further states that the yard is operated by B. Ronghe of Ronghe Estate, Ghatpimpri Road, who is also connected with the cold storage at Nandanvan. He states that residents who complained earlier were offered money to withdraw. The complainant has furnished photographs taken from his terrace which show two trucks and a covered stack of cartons. The photographs have been taken on record. Preliminary enquiry ordered before further action.

Complainant Digvijay Vaidyanathan, shopkeeper of 203, Sahastradhara Enclave, states that he was engaged as a supplier of stationery and printing to a concern named Girija Infra Consultants operating from 201, Girija Heights, Tilakwadi. He states that his bills remain unpaid since January and that on visiting the address he found the premises to be the residence of one Ishan Talapade, a freight broker, who told him that the consultancy was only a billing arrangement and that he should recover the money from a party in Nandanvan West. The complainant states that the said Talapade uses two mobile numbers, one being 9000014417, and that a grey Maruti Ertiga MP09BN1142 is parked at the premises. He further states that on 27/03/2026 while waiting outside he saw the said person receive a visitor in a silver Honda City whose number he noted as MP09CF8823. On enquiry with the society secretary the complainant learnt that no office of any consultancy is registered in the building. Complaint taken on record and documents called for from the registrar.

Complainant Pooja Ranmale, employed at a hotel in Vashisht Market Road and residing at 208, Vashisht Market Road, states that she had advanced a friendly loan of rupees sixty thousand to an acquaintance in November 2025 against a post dated cheque. On presentation on 06/04/2026 the cheque was returned unpaid with the endorsement funds insufficient. The complainant states that she issued a demand notice by registered post on 07/04/2026 which has been received but not replied to. She states that the borrower has since changed residence within the same locality and does not answer calls. The complainant produces the returned cheque, the bank memo and the postal acknowledgement. She states there is no other dispute between the parties and that she does not wish to make any allegation of criminal conspiracy. She has been advised regarding the procedure for filing before the competent magistrate and the limitation applicable thereto. Complaint recorded and copy furnished to the complainant. No cognizable offence made out at this stage.
